topic: Google Ads vs Meta Ads for Indian businesses
hook: Google Ads or Meta Ads? Wrong question. Here's the right one.
caption:
The real question isn't Google vs Meta.

It's: where is YOUR customer in their buying journey?

Google catches people who are actively searching. Meta catches people who don't know they need you yet.

Both work. But using the wrong one at the wrong time? That's how you burn your ad budget 🔥

Swipe for the complete breakdown → save for later 🔖

Tag a founder who's confused about where to spend their ad budget 👇

slides.title: Google vs Meta — Wrong Question
slides.body: The right question: Where is your customer in their journey? Searching for a solution? → Google. Scrolling, not looking? → Meta. This one distinction changes everything.

slides.title: Google Ads = Intent Capture
slides.body: Someone searches 'best AI voice agent India' — they WANT this. Google puts you in front of people with active purchase intent. High conversion, but limited volume.

slides.title: Meta Ads = Demand Creation
slides.body: Someone scrolls Instagram — they don't know they need you yet. Meta's algorithm finds people who LOOK LIKE your best customers and shows them your ad. Huge volume, lower intent.

slides.title: When to Use Google
slides.body: Your product solves a known problem. People search for your category. You want leads who are ready to buy NOW. Budget under ₹50K/month — start here for faster ROI.

slides.title: When to Use Meta
slides.body: You're building brand awareness. Your product is new or unique. You need visual storytelling to sell. You want massive reach in specific demographics.

slides.title: The Smart Move: Use Both
slides.body: Meta creates awareness → prospect searches on Google → your Google ad captures them. This full-funnel approach outperforms either platform alone by 40-60%.

slides.title: Our Clients' Average Results
slides.body: Google: ₹150-400 cost per lead. Meta: ₹80-250 cost per lead. Combined funnel: ₹100-300 CPL with 2x higher close rate. The numbers don't lie.

topic: 5 signs your website is killing your business
hook: Your website is losing you customers. Every. Single. Day.
caption:

slides.title: Your Website Might Be Killing Your Business
slides.body: 80% of Indian users browse on phones. If your site doesn't work perfectly on mobile, you're losing 4 out of 5 potential customers. That's not a minor issue — it's a disaster.

slides.title: Red Flag #1: Takes More Than 3 Seconds to Load
slides.body: 53% of mobile users abandon a site that takes over 3 seconds to load. Every additional second = 7% drop in conversions. Speed isn't a luxury — it's survival.

slides.title: Red Flag #2: Not Mobile-Optimized
slides.body: If visitors need to pinch and zoom on their phone, they'll leave and go to your competitor. Google also ranks mobile-unfriendly sites lower. Double penalty.

slides.title: Red Flag #3: No Clear Call to Action
slides.body: Visitors land on your homepage and think... now what? Every page needs ONE clear action: call, book, buy, download. No CTA = no conversions.

slides.title: Red Flag #4: Invisible to Google
slides.body: If your business doesn't appear on the first page of Google for your primary keywords, you effectively don't exist online. 75% of users never scroll past page 1.

slides.title: Red Flag #5: Looks Like It Was Built in 2019
slides.body: Design trends change. A dated website signals 'this business isn't keeping up.' Your competitors with modern sites look more trustworthy — even if your service is better.

slides.body:
